description:
# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access

description:
name: mockingjay_bypass_learn
doc: >
  Mockingjay with bypass learning: adds a Bypass History Sampler (BHS) to track

description:
# doc: Mockingjay with an added "Bypass Re-reference Predictor" to reduce wrong_bypass errors.
#      A 1-bit table `bypassed_reused_predictor` flags PC signatures that were recently
#      wrongly bypassed. A `last_bypassed_sig_per_hashed_set` table tracks the last bypassed
#      signature per a subset of sets to train the predictor. The `bypass_when` logic
#      dynamically adjusts the RDP threshold, making it harder to bypass lines with flagged PC signatures.
name: mockingjay_brp
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing. This version adds a Bypass Re-reference Predictor (BRP) to mitigate
  wrong_bypass errors. It uses `bypassed_reused_predictor` (1-bit per pc_sig) to flag
  signatures prone to wrong bypasses, and `last_bypassed_sig_per_hashed_set` to detect
  re-references of bypassed lines. The bypass decision is adapted by increasing the
  RDP threshold if the BRP flags the current access's PC signature.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    # Modify bypass condition using adjusted_rdp_threshold
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: {adjusted_rdp_threshold: {base_threshold: 73, brp_table: bypassed_reused_predictor, brp_index: pc_sig, brp_penalty_if_set: 5}}}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true
  - name: bypassed_reused_predictor # NEW: 1-bit table to flag PC_sigs prone to wrong_bypass
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 1                  # 0 or 1. 1 means "recently wrongly bypassed"
    init: ZERO
  - name: last_bypassed_sig_per_hashed_set # NEW: Stores PC_sig of last bypassed line for a subset of sets
    scope: global
    kind: counter
    entries: 256              # Hashed sets to fit budget (4096 / 16 = 256)
    width: 11                 # Same width as pc_sig
    init: ZERO

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    # NEW: If a miss occurs and its pc_sig matches the last bypassed sig for this hashed set,
    # it means a recently bypassed line was re-referenced. Flag this pc_sig in BRP.
    - when: {way: NUM_WAY} # If it's a miss
      when: {table: {table: last_bypassed_sig_per_hashed_set, index: {get_hashed_set_index: {modulo: 256}}, cmp: eq, threshold: {signature: pc_sig}}}
      train: {table: bypassed_reused_predictor, index: pc_sig, op: increment} # Set to 1 (saturating 1-bit counter)
    # NEW: If a line is inserted (not bypassed), reset its BRP flag.
    - when: {way: {cmp: lt, threshold: NUM_WAY}} # If it's an insertion (not a bypass)
      train: {table: bypassed_reused_predictor, index: pc_sig, op: decrement} # Set to 0 (saturating 1-bit counter)
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access
  # NEW: On a bypass (fill with way == NUM_WAY), record the pc_sig in the hashed set's table.
  - when: {way: NUM_WAY}
    set: {last_bypassed_sig_per_hashed_set: {index: {get_hashed_set_index: {modulo: 256}}, value: {signature: pc_sig}}}
new_words_text:
- name: get_hashed_set_index
  place: value
  params: {modulo: {int: [2, 4096]}}
  means: >
    Returns the current cache set index modulo the given 'modulo' value. This is used
    to hash the set index to a smaller range for table lookups.
- name: adjusted_rdp_threshold
  place: value
  params: {base_threshold: {int: [0, 127]}, brp_table: table, brp_index: signature, brp_penalty_if_set: {int: [0, 10]}}
  means: >
    Calculates an adjusted RDP threshold by adding 'brp_penalty_if_set' to 'base_threshold'
    if the entry in 'brp_table' at 'brp_index' is 1 (indicating a recent wrong_bypass for this signature);

# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access

# with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries

# train nothing.

# It introduces a small table, `bypassed_hits`, to record PC signatures of lines that were

name: mockingjay_bypassed_feedback

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter

  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none

    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}
    - {table: {table: bypassed_hits, index: pc_sig, cmp: gte, threshold: 1}} # Do not bypass if previously useful after bypass

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true
  - name: bypassed_hits       # New table to track useful bypassed lines
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048             # Same size as RDP table for consistency
    width: 2                  # Small counter (0-3) to indicate usefulness
    init: ZERO
    unset: true               # Entries start as absent/zero

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
      - {name: bypassed_flag, kind: flag, width: 1, init: ZERO} # New flag to mark if this line was bypassed
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}

      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true

        set: {bypassed_flag: {const: 0}}                                 # Reset flag after feedback

        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install:
      signature: {signature: pc_sig}
      timestamp: {read: set_clock}

    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access
  - when: {way: NUM_WAY} # If the fill was bypassed (way is NUM_WAY)
    each_way:
      when: {counter: {counter: set_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 0}} # dummy condition to run on sampler
      set: {bypassed_flag: {const: 1}} # Mark the corresponding sampler entry as bypassed
    # The new word approach is not needed here; bypassed_flag is a sampler field
    # and can be set directly when a fill is bypassed. However, the sampler only
    # sees the *current* fill, not the *bypassed* fill.
    # The sampler does not get an `on_fill` event for bypassed lines directly.
    # The `on_match` of the sampler would need to detect a hit on a line that *was* bypassed.
    # The current `bypassed_flag` is per sampler entry, not per line in the LLC.
    # To track bypassed lines that are later accessed, we need to mark them *at the point of bypass*.
    # A bypassed fill doesn't have a `way` in the cache, but it does have an `ip` (for pc_sig).
    # The `sampled_cache`'s `install` is called for *fills*, not for bypasses.
    # The `on_match` is called for *hits*.
    #
    # The problem is: how does the sampler know a line was bypassed when it later sees a hit?
    #
    # Let's adjust:
    # 1. When a fill is bypassed, we update the `bypassed_hits` table by decrementing the counter
    #    for the current pc_sig, indicating a 'bad' bypass.
    # 2. When a hit occurs, we update the `bypassed_hits` table by incrementing the counter
    #    for the current pc_sig, indicating a 'good' access (which might have been a bypass).
    # This might be too aggressive. The original suggestion was "which bypassed lines proved useful".
    # This means a line was bypassed, then later *accessed* (hit or miss, but not filled).
    #
    # The sampler can track this: when a line is installed in the sampler, mark it as 'not bypassed'.
    # If the *actual* LLC fill was bypassed, we need a way to tell the sampler.
    #
    # Current `on_fill` has `when: {way: NUM_WAY}` for a bypassed fill.
    # If a fill is bypassed, its `pc_sig` is known.
    # We want to train `bypassed_hits` when a line is bypassed *and then later hit*.
    #
    # The `bypassed_flag` in the sampler seems correct if the sampler's `install` is aware of the bypass decision.
    # However, `install` runs *before* the `bypass_when` condition for the actual LLC fill.
    #
    # Let's use the `on_fill` event for bypassed fills to update the `bypassed_hits` table directly.
    # And then `on_hit` to update it if the hit was on a line that *could have been* bypassed but wasn't.
    #
    # A simpler approach for `wrong_bypass`:
    # 1. When a fill is bypassed, mark its `pc_sig` in `bypassed_hits` with a 'bypassed' state (e.g., set to 1).
    # 2. On a subsequent hit *to that signature*, if it was marked 'bypassed', increment the counter.
    # 3. Clear the 'bypassed' state after some time or on a hit.
    #
    # The `bypassed_hits` table is for *signatures*, not specific lines.
    #
    # Let's refine the bypass feedback logic:
    # `bypassed_hits` stores a confidence for *not bypassing* a given `pc_sig`.
    # - If a fill *is* bypassed, we decrement `bypassed_hits[pc_sig]`. This means the bypass was chosen, so we reinforce the bypass decision, or punish the predictor.
    # - If a fill *is NOT* bypassed (i.e., installed), and it later gets a hit, we increment `bypassed_hits[pc_sig]`. This means it was a useful line that we should not have bypassed.
    #
    # This is the "wrong_bypass" feedback.
    #
    # Re-evaluating the `bypassed_flag` in the sampler:
    # It's intended to mark a sampler entry as representing a line that *was* bypassed in the LLC.
    # `install` for the sampler always happens. The `bypassed_flag` can only be set if the `on_fill` event in the *main* policy
    # communicates the bypass decision to the sampler.
    #
    # Let's define a new word for this. A step word that takes the sampler and a flag to set.
    #
    # New word: `mark_sampler_bypassed`
    # - name: mark_sampler_bypassed
    #   place: step
    #   params: {sampler: sampler, flag_field: sampler_field}
    #   means: >
    #     For the current access, if the sampler finds a matching entry, set the specified flag_field in that entry to 1.
    #     If no match, do nothing. This is called when the LLC bypasses a line.
    #
    # This new word would be used in `on_fill` when `way == NUM_WAY`.
    # The `on_match` in the sampler would then check this `bypassed_flag`.

    # Okay, let's try the simpler approach without a new word first, as the prompt discourages new words unless strictly necessary.
    # The issue is how to tell the sampler that an installed entry corresponds to a bypassed line.
    # The sampler's `install` happens on *every* fill, whether bypassed or not.
    # The `bypassed_flag` in the sampler's `fields` is a good idea.
    # But how to set it correctly for bypassed LLC fills?
    #
    # The `on_fill` event with `way == NUM_WAY` means the LLC *did* bypass.
    # We need to update the sampler's *installed* entry for *this* access to indicate it was bypassed.
    # But the sampler's `install` already happened, creating the entry.
    # And `on_fill` cannot directly modify sampler entries for the current fill's `pc_sig` other than through `sample`.
    #
    # Let's rethink. If a line is bypassed, it means it was *not* installed in the LLC.
    # The sampler, however, *always* installs an entry for any `on_fill` event.
    # So the sampler entry for a bypassed line will exist.
    #
    # The `bypassed_flag` field in the sampler is meant to indicate that the *LLC* line it represents was bypassed.
    # When `on_fill` is called, if `way == NUM_WAY`, it means the LLC bypassed.
    # At this point, the sampler *has already processed* its `install` for this line.
    # So, we need a way to tell the sampler that its *just installed* entry for this `pc_sig` should be marked as bypassed.
    #
    # The `after` section of the sampler runs *after* installation.
    # But `after` cannot access the `way` of the main cache.
    #
    # The `on_fill` event can `sample` the `sampled_cache` *again* after the bypass decision.
    # But `sample` would either hit or install. We need to specifically modify the *just installed* entry.
    #
    # This is where a new word or a specific mechanism is needed.
    # The prompt explicitly suggests a new word to track hits on non-resident lines.
    #
    # Let's try to define a new word that acts on the sampler's *last installed entry* for the current access,
    # or perhaps by finding the current access's entry.

    # Alternative strategy:
    # 1. When a fill is bypassed, increment `bypassed_hits[pc_sig]`. This implies "this signature was bypassed, and we should track if it's useful".
    # 2. When a hit occurs, *decrement* `bypassed_hits[pc_sig]` if it's > 0. This implies "this signature was useful, so maybe don't bypass next time".
    #
    # This means `bypassed_hits` acts as a counter for "how many times was this signature bypassed and then later hit before eviction?".
    # A high value means "don't bypass".
    #
    # Let's try this simpler approach first, without a new word, by modifying `on_fill` and `on_hit`.

    # `bypassed_hits` table:
    # - Value 0: no history or consistently bypassed and not reused.
    # - Value > 0: has been bypassed and then reused.
    #
    # `on_fill` (when bypassed): if a fill is bypassed, we just made a decision.
    # We don't know yet if it was a 'wrong_bypass'. That's determined by future hits.
    # So, `on_fill` for a bypass should *not* update `bypassed_hits` in a way that affects *this* bypass decision.
    #
    # The `wrong_bypass` mistake is: "bypassed a line reused before every resident line".
    # This means a line *was bypassed*, but it *should have been kept*.
    #
    # The `bypassed_hits` table should reflect signatures for which bypass was a *bad idea*.
    # So, if a line with a certain pc_sig is *bypassed*, and then later *hit* (while not in cache, which is impossible to track directly),
    # or just *hit* in the sampler, then we should punish the bypass decision for that pc_sig.
    #
    # Let's use the sampler. The sampler *always* installs an entry for a fill.
    # In `sampler.install`, we can set a `bypassed_flag`.
    # But `install` doesn't know if the LLC *actually* bypassed.
    #
    # The only way to get feedback on `wrong_bypass` is to track signatures of *bypassed* lines.
    #
    # Let's define a new word: `mark_bypassed_sampler_entry`.
    # This word will be called *after* the bypass decision is made in `on_fill`.
    # It will find the entry in the sampler corresponding to the current access's `pc_sig` and `line_address` (tag),
    # and set its `bypassed_flag`.
    #
    # This is complex. Let's simplify the feedback mechanism for `bypassed_hits`.
    #
    # `bypassed_hits` is a table of `pc_sig` -> "confidence to *not* bypass".
    #
    # - `on_fill` (if bypassed): We decided to bypass. This was potentially a mistake.
    #   But we only know it's a mistake if it's reused. So, *don't* update `bypassed_hits` here.
    #
    # - `on_hit`: A line was useful. If its `pc_sig` has a `bypassed_hits` entry > 0,
    #   it suggests it was previously bypassed (or could have been) and was useful.
    #   So, increment `bypassed_hits[pc_sig]`.
    #
    # - `sampler.on_match`: If a sampler entry was marked `bypassed_flag=1`, and it's a hit,

# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,

name: mockingjay_bypass_feedback
doc: >
  Mockingjay, enhanced to learn from wrong_bypass errors. A new global_clock and a
  small bypass_history_sampler track bypassed lines. When a previously bypassed
  line is re-accessed, the RDP table is trained: decremented if the reuse was
  'too soon' (wrong bypass), and incremented if 'late' (correct bypass).
  This addresses the wrong_bypass errors observed in previous feedback.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO
  - name: global_clock
    scope: global
    kind: counter
    width: 64
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}

        free: true

        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:

    extra_index_bits: 0
    ways: 1

  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}

        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}

    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_access:
  - set: {global_clock: {add: 1}} # Increment global clock on every access

      pc_signature: pc_sig
      current_time: global_clock

on_hit:

      target_sampler: bypass_history_sampler
      rdp_table: rdp
      pc_signature: pc_sig
      current_time: global_clock
      wrong_bypass_rd_threshold: 73
      is_bypassed_fill: 1 # This is a bypassed fill event
new_words_text:
- name: process_bypass_feedback
  place: step
  params:
    target_sampler: sampler # The bypass_history_sampler instance
    rdp_table: table # The RDP table
    pc_signature: signature # Current access's PC signature (used for install)
    current_time: state # The global_clock counter
    wrong_bypass_rd_threshold: {int: [0, 127]} # Reuse dist below this is wrong
    is_bypassed_fill: {int: [0, 1]} # 1 if current event is a bypassed fill, 0 otherwise
  means: >
    This step manages feedback for bypass decisions.
    First, it attempts to find an entry in target_sampler matching the current line address.
    If a match is found (meaning a previously bypassed line is being reaccessed):
      It calculates the elapsed time: current_time - matched_entry.timestamp.
      If this elapsed time is less than wrong_bypass_rd_threshold, it means a wrong bypass
      occurred. The rdp_table entry for the matched_entry.signature is decremented by 1
      (saturating at 0).
      Otherwise (a correct bypass), the rdp_table entry for matched_entry.signature is
      incremented by 1 (saturating at MAX).
      The matched entry in target_sampler is then freed.
    Second, if is_bypassed_fill is 1:
      A new entry is installed in target_sampler for the current line address,
      using pc_signature as its signature and current_time as its timestamp.
      If the sampler set is full, target_sampler's victim policy is used to evict an old entry.

description:
# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

  This design adds a small `bypassed_history` sampler to track bypassed lines and
  train the RDP. This addresses `wrong_bypass` errors by decrementing the RDP if a
  bypassed line is later reused, and incrementing if it's evicted from the tracker
  without reuse. A global clock was added for the tracker's LRU policy.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO
  - name: global_clock        # NEW: Global clock for bypassed_history sampler's age
    scope: global
    kind: counter
    width: 64
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

  - name: bypassed_history     # NEW: Sampler to track bypassed lines and provide feedback to RDP
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}        # Sampled sets for bypassed history, same as sampled_cache
    extra_index_bits: 0       # No extra indexing for simplicity
    ways: 1                   # Smallest possible: 1 way per sampler set
    tag_bits: 46              # Full line address tag for precise matching
    fields:
      - {name: pc_sig_bypassed, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp_bypassed, kind: counter, width: 64, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: global_clock, stamp: timestamp_bypassed}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true} # LRU victim policy
    on_match:                 # A previously bypassed line was subsequently reused (wrong_bypass)
      - train: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig_bypassed, op: decrement} # Penalize bypass decision
      - free: true            # Remove from tracker as it's no longer 'bypassed and un-reused'
    on_replace:               # A bypassed line was evicted from tracker without being reused (good_bypass)
      - train: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig_bypassed, op: increment} # Reward bypass decision
    install: {pc_sig_bypassed: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp_bypassed: {tick: global_clock}}


procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_access:
  - set: {global_clock: {add: 1}} # NEW: Increment global clock on every access
  - sample: bypassed_history  # NEW: Check if current access hits a bypassed entry
  - run: access               # Original Mockingjay access procedure

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - when: {type_not_in: [WRITE]} # NEW: Only non-writes can be bypassed by policy
    when: {way: NUM_WAY}      # NEW: If the fill was bypassed
    sample: bypassed_history  # NEW: Install the bypassed line into the tracker
  - run: access

description:
# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}

description:
name: mockingjay_bypass_feedback
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

  This version adds a bypass feedback mechanism. A new signature, pc_sig_base,
  captures the IP and prefetch bit, but not the hit bit, allowing tracking of a PC
  regardless of hit/miss status. A new table, bypass_misprediction_counter, stores
  how often a given pc_sig_base has been involved in a wrong bypass. When a line is
  bypassed, this counter is incremented for its pc_sig_base. When a line hits, if
  its pc_sig_base had a non-zero entry in the counter, it means a previous bypass
  for this PC was likely a misprediction, so the counter is decremented. The bypass
  decision itself is now conditioned: a line is bypassed only if the RDP predicts a
  long reuse distance AND the bypass_misprediction_counter for that PC_base is low
  (meaning bypasses for this PC are generally reliable).

  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    # Original RDP high prediction, now conditioned by bypass_misprediction_counter
    - conditional_bypass_rdp_threshold:
        rdp_table: rdp
        rdp_index: pc_sig
        rdp_cmp: gt
        rdp_threshold: 73
        mispred_table: bypass_misprediction_counter
        mispred_index: pc_sig_base
        mispred_cmp: lte # Bypass only if misprediction counter is low (0 or 1)
        mispred_threshold: 1 # Threshold 1 means bypass if counter is 0 or 1. If 2 or 3, don't bypass.

    low_bits: 11

    max: 95                   # INF_RD

description:
# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay_bypasstracker
doc: >
  Mockingjay with a bypass tracker: Reduced the main sampler's ways to free up budget.
  Added a small `bypassed_lines_sampler` to track recently bypassed lines.
  When a line that was previously bypassed is accessed (a miss), it decrements the RDP entry for its signature (wrong_bypass).
  When a bypassed line is evicted from the `bypassed_lines_sampler` without being re-accessed, it increments the RDP entry (should_bypass).
  This improves the RDP's accuracy for bypass decisions, addressing `wrong_bypass` and `should_bypass` errors.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 3                   # Reduced from 5 to free up budget for bypass tracker
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

  - name: bypassed_lines_sampler # New sampler to track recently bypassed lines
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}        # Sampled sets for this tracker
    extra_index_bits: 1       # 2 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 2                   # Two entries per sampler set
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: used, kind: flag, width: 1, init: ZERO} # Tracks if the bypassed line was re-accessed
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO} # For age-based victim
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      # If a previously bypassed line is accessed again (miss in LLC), it was a wrong_bypass.
      # Decrement RDP for this signature to discourage future bypasses.
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: decrement}
      - set: {used: {const: 1}} # Mark as used
      - set: {timestamp: {read: set_clock}} # Update timestamp
    on_replace:
      # If a bypassed line is evicted from this sampler without being used, it was a should_bypass.
      # Increment RDP for its signature to encourage future bypasses.
      - when: {counter: {counter: used, cmp: eq, threshold: 0}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install:
      # On a bypassed fill, record the signature and mark as unused.
      {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, used: {const: 0}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - sample: bypassed_lines_sampler # Sample the bypass tracker on every access
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - when: {way: NUM_WAY} # If this is a bypassed fill (fill event with way == NUM_WAY)
    sample: bypassed_lines_sampler # Install the bypassed line's signature into the tracker
    stop: true # Stop processing for this fill, as no line was installed into the LLC
  - run: access # For non-bypassed fills, run the normal access procedure to set ETR

description:
# Mockingjay with a Bypass Feedback Mechanism (BFM) to reduce wrong_bypass errors.

name: mockingjay_bfm
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.
  This design adds a Bypass Feedback Mechanism (BFM) using a small bypassed_tracker
  sampler. When a line is bypassed, its PC signature and address are recorded in the
  bypassed_tracker. If this tracked line is accessed again, it signifies a wrong_bypass
  event, and the RDP table for that PC signature is decremented, making future bypasses
  for that signature less likely.

  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO
  - name: global_clock        # Added for Bypass Feedback Mechanism
    scope: global
    kind: counter
    width: 64
    init: ZERO

  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none

    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}

# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay_bypasstrack
doc: >
  Mockingjay with a Bypassed Signature Tracker (BST). The BST is a small sampler that
  records PC signatures of lines that were bypassed. If a line is subsequently filled
  and its signature matches an entry in the BST, it indicates a previous wrong bypass.
  The RDP table is then decremented for that signature, making future bypass decisions
  less aggressive.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 16}        # Small number of sets for tracking
    extra_index_bits: 0       # No extra index bits, direct mapping of set to sampler set
    ways: 2                   # 2 ways per set
    tag_bits: 10              # Use a portion of the line address as tag
    fields:
      - {name: pc_sig_bypassed, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: install_time, kind: counter, width: 64, init: ZERO} # To track age for victim
    age: {clock: access_count, stamp: install_time} # Use global access_count for aging
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: pc_sig_bypassed, cmp: eq, threshold: {signature: pc_sig}}} # Match on signature
        train: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig_bypassed, op: decrement} # Wrong bypass: make RDP less aggressive
        free: true # Remove from tracker, it's now resident
    install: {pc_sig_bypassed: {signature: pc_sig}, install_time: {tick: access_count}} # Store bypassed signature

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  # Check if this fill is a line that was previously bypassed
  - when: {way: {cmp: ne, threshold: NUM_WAY}} # Only if this fill is NOT a bypass
    sample: bypassed_sig_tracker # Check if the current signature was previously bypassed
  - run: access
  # If the fill was bypassed, record its signature in the tracker
  - when: {way: {cmp: eq, threshold: NUM_WAY}} # If the fill was bypassed
    sample: bypassed_sig_tracker # Install the bypassed signature into the tracker

description:
# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true
  - name: bypassed_reaccess_tracker
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048 # Example size: 2048 entries * 4 bits = 1KB. Adjust as needed.
    width: 4      # e.g., 4 bits to count up to 15 re-accesses. Adjust as needed.
    init: ZERO
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}

      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}

        free: true

      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:

    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}

description:
# Reference: DPC4-ChampSim/replacement/mockingjay, single-core build. Sizes are for
# the DPC4 LLC, 4096 x 12: INF_RD 95, INF_ETR 11, MAX_RD 73, 11-bit signatures,
# 32 sampled sets. The multi-core build folds the core id instead of the hit bit,
# inserts an unknown signature at INF_ETR, and scales prefetch samples by less.
name: mockingjay
doc: >
  Mockingjay: each line holds an estimated time to reuse (ETR), counted down every
  8 accesses to its set; the victim is the line with the largest |ETR|, an overdue
  (negative) one on ties. A predictor table keyed by the hit-or-miss PC signature
  gives the ETR on insertion, and a fill predicted to be reused after every line in
  the set is bypassed. A sampled shadow cache on 32 sets measures reuse distances
  with an 8-bit per-set clock and trains the predictor one step at a time; entries
  older than INF_RD train it up as scans. Writebacks are inserted at -INF_ETR and
  train nothing.

state:
  - name: etr
    scope: per_line
    kind: signed
    width: 5                  # holds -11..11
    init: 0
  - name: etr_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 4
    init: 8                   # GRANULARITY: the first access to a set ages it
  - name: set_clock
    scope: per_set
    kind: counter
    width: 8                  # TIMESTAMP_BITS; wraps by design
    init: ZERO

victim:
  key: etr
  extremum: max_magnitude
  tie_break: prefer_negative
  on_search: none
  bypass_when:                # the incoming line is predicted to be reused after every resident
    - {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
    - {table_exceeds_victim: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

signatures:
  - name: pc_sig
    source: ip
    fold: [hit, prefetch]
    hash: crc3
    low_bits: 11

tables:
  - name: rdp
    scope: global
    kind: saturating
    entries: 2048
    width: 7
    max: 95                   # INF_RD
    unset: true

samplers:
  - name: sampled_cache
    scope: global
    sets: {mirror: 32}
    extra_index_bits: 4       # 16 sampler sets per sampled set
    ways: 5
    tag_bits: 10
    fields:
      - {name: signature, kind: counter, width: 11, init: ZERO}
      - {name: timestamp, kind: counter, width: 8, init: ZERO}
    age: {clock: set_clock, stamp: timestamp}
    victim: {key: age, extremum: max, tie_break: first, prefer_free: true}
    on_match:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        stop: true            # too old to be a reuse distance; the sweep detrains it
      - when: {type_in: [PREFETCH]}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, scale: 2, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
        stop: true
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: toward, sample: age, min_diff: 16}
        free: true
    sweep:
      - when: {counter: {counter: age, cmp: gt, threshold: 95}}
        train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
        free: true
    on_replace:
      - train: {table: rdp, index: signature, op: increment}
    install: {signature: {signature: pc_sig}, timestamp: {read: set_clock}}
    after:
      - set: {set_clock: {add: 1}}

procedures:
  access:                     # mockingjay.cc access(): the update body shared by hits and fills
    - sample: sampled_cache
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      each_way:
        except_touched: true
        when: {counter: {counter: etr, cmp: lt, threshold: 11, abs: true}}
        set: {etr: {add: -1}}
    - when: {counter: {counter: etr_clock, cmp: eq, threshold: 8}}
      set: {etr_clock: {const: 0}}
    - set: {etr_clock: {add: 1}}
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: absent}}
      set: {etr: {const: 0}}
      stop: true
    - when: {table: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, cmp: gt, threshold: 73}}
      set: {etr: {const: 11}}
      stop: true
    - set: {etr: {table: rdp, index: pc_sig, div: 8}}

on_hit:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    stop: true
  - run: access

on_fill:
  - when: {type_in: [WRITE]}
    set: {etr: {const: -11}}
    stop: true
  - run: access
